source.primary_witnesses: MT BHS Codex Leningradensis — entirely Hebrew. **LANGUAGE RETURN**: chapter 8 returns to Hebrew (the Aramaic core 2:4b–7:28 has ended). SECONDARY: 4Q113 (Danielb) preserves fragments of ch 8. TERTIARY: OG-Greek + Theodotion-Greek consulted at text-critical cruxes, especially v 9 (the little-horn-from-one-of-them) + vv 11-14 (the daily-sacrifice + 2300 evenings-mornings).
source.transliteration_convention: SBL Hebrew convention throughout (Tiberian vocalization per Codex Leningradensis; ʾ for aleph; ʿ for ayin; ḥ for ḥet; ə for shewa; doubled consonants for dagesh forte).
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against BHS apparatus + DJD XVI 2000 + Ziegler-Munnich 1999.
source.fetchedFrom: BHS; Ulrich DJD XVI 2000; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999.
source.citation: BHS (Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft 1997); Ulrich et al. 2000 DJD XVI; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999 Septuaginta XVI.2; 1 Macc 1.
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 8 — HEBREW, the ram and the male goat. The most explicitly historicizable vision in Daniel: the ram = Medo-Persia, the male goat = Greece (named in v 21 — יָוָן Yāwān), and the little horn = Antiochus IV Epiphanes (recognized by consensus). The chronological focus is the persecution-of-167-164 BCE: the abolition of the *tāmîd* (daily burnt-offering) and the desecration of the Temple. The 2300 evenings-mornings calendrical figure (v 14) anchors the persecution-chronology and is the foundational Daniel calendar-arithmetic problem.

verses.text: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁל֔וֹשׁ לְמַלְכ֖וּת בֵּלְאשַׁצַּ֣ר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ חָז֞וֹן נִרְאָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ אֲנִ֣י דָנִיֵּ֔אל אַחֲרֵ֛י הַנִּרְאָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י בַּתְּחִלָּֽה׃
verses.translit: bi-šnaṯ šālōš lə-malḵūṯ Bēlšaʾṣṣar ham-meleḵ ḥāzōn nirʾāh ʾēlay ʾănî Dāniyyēʾl ʾaḥărê han-nirʾāh ʾēlay bat-təḥillāh
verses.notes: **In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after that which appeared to me at the first.** **LANGUAGE RETURN TO HEBREW**: this is the first word in Hebrew since 2:4a. **DATING**: the third year of Belshazzar = c. 550 BCE (if Belshazzar's regency began 553). The 'first vision' = ch 7's vision in Belshazzar's first year.

verses.text: וָאֶרְאֶה֮ בֶּחָזוֹן֒ וַיְהִי֙ בִּרְאֹתִ֔י וַאֲנִי֙ בְּשׁוּשַׁ֣ן הַבִּירָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵילָ֣ם הַמְּדִינָ֑ה וָאֶרְאֶה֙ בֶּֽחָז֔וֹן וַאֲנִ֥י הָיִ֖יתִי עַל־אוּבַ֥ל אוּלָֽי׃
verses.translit: wā-ʾerʾeh be-ḥāzōn way-hî bi-rʾōṯî wa-ʾănî bə-Šūšan hab-bîrāh ʾăšer bə-ʿÊlām ham-məḏînāh wā-ʾerʾeh be-ḥāzōn wa-ʾănî hāyîṯî ʿal-ʾūḇal ʾŪlāy
verses.notes: **I saw in the vision; and when I saw, I was in Susa the capital, which is in the province of Elam; and I saw in the vision, and I was at the river Ulai.** **GEOGRAPHY**: Susa (Šūšan) — the Elamite/Persian capital (modern Shush, Iran); the *Ulai* river (Akkadian Eulaeus, modern Karkheh) flowed past Susa. Daniel is *visionarily* present, not physically. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Ezek 1, 8 (Ezekiel transported in vision); cf. Rev 17:3, 21:10 ('he carried me away in the spirit').

verses.text: וָאֶשָּׂ֤א עֵינַי֙ וָאֶרְאֶ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֣ה ׀ אַ֣יִל אֶחָ֗ד עֹמֵ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י הָאֻבָ֖ל וְל֣וֹ קְרָנָ֑יִם וְהַקְּרָנַ֣יִם גְּבֹה֗וֹת וְהָאַחַת֙ גְּבֹהָ֣ה מִן־הַשֵּׁנִ֔ית וְהַ֨גְּבֹהָ֔ה עֹלָ֖ה בָּאַחֲרֹנָֽה׃
verses.translit: wā-ʾeśśāʾ ʿênay wā-ʾerʾeh wə-hinnēh ʾayil ʾeḥāḏ ʿōmēḏ lip̄nê hā-ʾuḇāl wə-lō qərānāyim wə-haq-qərānayim gəḇōhōṯ wə-hā-ʾaḥaṯ gəḇōhāh min-haš-šēnîṯ wə-hag-gəḇōhāh ʿōlāh bā-ʾaḥărōnāh
verses.notes: **I raised my eyes and saw, and behold, a ram standing on the bank of the river. It had two horns; and both horns were high, but one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up last.** **THE RAM = MEDO-PERSIA** (explicit in v 20). The unequal horns = Media (older, lower) + Persia (later, higher) — Cyrus's Persian element overtook the Median element.

verses.text: רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת־הָאַ֡יִל מְנַגֵּחַ֩ יָ֨מָּה וְצָפ֜וֹנָה וָנֶ֗גְבָּה וְכָל־חַיּוֹת֙ לֹֽא־יַֽעַמְד֣וּ לְפָנָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּ֖יל מִיָּד֑וֹ וְעָשָׂ֥ה כִרְצוֹנ֖וֹ וְהִגְדִּֽיל׃
verses.translit: rāʾîṯî ʾeṯ-hā-ʾayil mə-naggēaḥ yāmmāh wə-ṣāp̄ōnāh wā-neḡbāh wə-ḵol-ḥayyōṯ lōʾ-yaʿamḏū lə-p̄ānāyw wə-ʾên maṣṣîl mî-yāḏō wə-ʿāśāh ḵi-rṣōnō wə-hiḡdîl
verses.notes: **I saw the ram charging westward and northward and southward; no beast could stand before him, and there was no one who could rescue from his power; he did as he pleased and became great.** Persian expansion: west (Babylon, Asia Minor), north (Caucasus), south (Egypt). Notably no eastward expansion mentioned (Persia's east was secured early by Cyrus).

verses.text: וַאֲנִ֣י ׀ הָיִ֣יתִי מֵבִ֗ין וְהִנֵּ֤ה צְפִיר־הָֽעִזִּים֙ בָּ֤א מִן־הַֽמַּעֲרָב֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֵ֥ין נוֹגֵ֖עַ בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְהַ֨צָּפִ֔יר קֶ֥רֶן חָז֖וּת בֵּ֥ין עֵינָֽיו׃
verses.translit: wa-ʾănî hāyîṯî mēḇîn wə-hinnēh ṣəp̄îr-hā-ʿizzîm bāʾ min-ham-maʿărāḇ ʿal-pənê ḵol-hā-ʾāreṣ wə-ʾên nōḡēaʿ bā-ʾāreṣ wə-haṣ-ṣāp̄îr qeren ḥāzūṯ bên ʿênāyw
verses.notes: **As I was considering, behold, a male goat came from the west across the face of the whole earth, without touching the ground; and the goat had a conspicuous horn between his eyes.** **THE MALE GOAT = GREECE** (explicit v 21). **THE CONSPICUOUS HORN = ALEXANDER THE GREAT**. The 'not touching the ground' suggests the speed of Alexander's conquest (333-323 BCE).

verses.text: וַיָּבֹ֗א עַד־הָאַ֙יִל֙ בַּ֣עַל הַקְּרָנַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאִ֔יתִי עֹמֵ֖ד לִפְנֵ֣י הָאֻבָ֑ל וַיָּ֥רָץ אֵלָ֖יו בַּחֲמַ֥ת כֹּחֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: way-yāḇōʾ ʿaḏ-hā-ʾayil baʿal haq-qərānayim ʾăšer rāʾîṯî ʿōmēḏ lip̄nê hā-ʾuḇāl way-yāroṣ ʾēlāyw ba-ḥămaṯ kōḥō
verses.notes: **He came to the ram with the two horns, which I had seen standing on the bank of the river, and he ran at him in his mighty wrath.**

verses.text: וּרְאִיתִ֞יו מַגִּ֣יעַ ׀ אֵ֣צֶל הָאַ֗יִל וַיִּתְמַרְמַ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ וַיַּ֣ךְ אֶת־הָאַ֔יִל וַיְשַׁבֵּר֙ אֶת־שְׁתֵּ֣י קְרָנָ֔יו וְלֹא־הָ֥יָה כֹ֛חַ בָּאַ֖יִל לַעֲמֹ֣ד לְפָנָ֑יו וַיַּשְׁלִיכֵ֤הוּ אַ֙רְצָה֙ וַֽיִּרְמְסֵ֔הוּ וְלֹא־הָיָ֥ה מַצִּ֛יל לָאַ֖יִל מִיָּדֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: ū-rəʾîṯîw maggîaʿ ʾēṣel hā-ʾayil way-yiṯmarmar ʾēlāyw way-yaḵ ʾeṯ-hā-ʾayil way-šabbēr ʾeṯ-šətê qərānāyw wə-lōʾ-hāyāh ḵōaḥ bā-ʾayil la-ʿămōḏ lə-p̄ānāyw way-yašlîḵēhū ʾarṣāh way-yirməsēhū wə-lōʾ-hāyāh maṣṣîl lā-ʾayil mî-yāḏō
verses.notes: **I saw him come close to the ram, and he was enraged against him and struck the ram and broke his two horns; and the ram had no power to stand before him, but he cast him down to the ground and trampled him; and there was no one who could rescue the ram from his power.** Alexander's decisive defeat of Darius III at Issus (333 BCE) and Gaugamela (331 BCE).

verses.text: וּצְפִ֥יר הָעִזִּ֖ים הִגְדִּ֣יל עַד־מְאֹ֑ד וּכְעָצְמ֗וֹ נִשְׁבְּרָה֙ הַקֶּ֣רֶן הַגְּדוֹלָ֔ה וַֽתַּעֲלֶ֜נָה חָז֤וּת אַרְבַּע֙ תַּחְתֶּ֔יהָ לְאַרְבַּ֖ע רוּח֥וֹת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
verses.translit: ū-ṣəp̄îr hā-ʿizzîm hiḡdîl ʿaḏ-məʾōḏ ū-ḵə-ʿoṣmō nišbərāh haq-qeren hag-gəḏōlāh wat-taʿălenāh ḥāzūṯ ʾarbaʿ taḥtêhā lə-ʾarbaʿ rūḥōṯ haš-šāmāyim
verses.notes: **Then the male goat grew exceedingly great; but when he was strong, the great horn was broken, and instead of it there came up four conspicuous horns toward the four winds of heaven.** **ALEXANDER'S DEATH (323 BCE) + THE FOUR DIADOCHI**: the four successor-kingdoms = Ptolemies (Egypt), Seleucids (Syria/Babylonia), Antigonids (Macedonia), Lysimachus/Cassander/Attalids — the partitioning of Alexander's empire.

verses.text: וּמִן־הָאַחַ֣ת מֵהֶ֔ם יָצָ֥א קֶֽרֶן־אַחַ֖ת מִצְּעִירָ֑ה וַתִּגְדַּל־יֶ֛תֶר אֶל־הַנֶּ֥גֶב וְאֶל־הַמִּזְרָ֖ח וְאֶל־הַצֶּֽבִי׃
verses.translit: ū-min-hā-ʾaḥaṯ mēhem yāṣāʾ qeren-ʾaḥaṯ miṣ-ṣəʿîrāh wat-tiḡdal-yeṯer ʾel-han-neḡeḇ wə-ʾel-ham-mizrāḥ wə-ʾel-haṣ-ṣeḇî
verses.witness_tertiary: OG presents 'one strong horn' instead of 'a little horn'; Theodotion preserves 'a little horn' agreeing with MT
verses.notes: **Out of one of them came forth a little horn, which grew exceedingly great toward the south, toward the east, and toward the glorious land.** **THE LITTLE HORN = ANTIOCHUS IV EPIPHANES** (Seleucid king, 175-164 BCE; from the Seleucid quarter of Alexander's diadochi). **'TOWARD THE SOUTH'** = the Sixth Syrian War against Ptolemaic Egypt (169-168 BCE). **'TOWARD THE EAST'** = the Parthian campaigns. **'THE GLORIOUS LAND'** (הַצֶּבִי haṣ-ṣeḇî 'the beauty' = Judea) — cf. 11:16, 11:41, Jer 3:19, Ezek 20:6, 15. The persecution of Judea begins in 167 BCE.

verses.text: וַתִּגְדַּ֖ל עַד־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַתַּפֵּ֥ל אַ֛רְצָה מִן־הַצָּבָ֥א וּמִן־הַכּוֹכָבִ֖ים וַֽתִּרְמְסֵֽם׃
verses.translit: wat-tiḡdal ʿaḏ-ṣəḇāʾ haš-šāmāyim wat-tappēl ʾarṣāh min-haṣ-ṣāḇāʾ ū-min-hak-kōḵāḇîm wat-tirməsēm
verses.notes: **It grew great, even to the host of heaven; and some of the host of the stars it cast down to the ground, and trampled upon them.** **THE HOST OF HEAVEN + THE STARS**: cosmic-symbolic for the persecution of the saints. The 'stars' = the righteous (cf. 12:3 'they shall shine like the stars'); the angelic-army (cf. 1 Kgs 22:19). **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Rev 12:4 ('its tail swept down a third of the stars of heaven and cast them to the earth') — direct Dan 8:10 inheritance. cf. Isa 14:13 (the day-star's hubris).

verses.text: וְעַ֥ד שַֽׂר־הַצָּבָ֖א הִגְדִּ֑יל וּמִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ הרים הוּרַ֣ם הַתָּמִ֔יד וְהֻשְׁלַ֖ךְ מְכ֥וֹן מִקְדָּשֽׁוֹ׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿaḏ śar-haṣ-ṣāḇāʾ hiḡdîl ū-mim-mennū hūram hat-tāmîḏ wə-hušlaḵ məḵōn miqdāšō
verses.notes: **It magnified itself, even to the prince of the host; and the continual burnt offering was taken away from him, and the place of his sanctuary was overthrown.** **THE PRINCE OF THE HOST** (שַׂר־הַצָּבָא śar-haṣ-ṣāḇāʾ) = either Michael (cf. 12:1, 10:13) OR a direct theophanic title for YHWH. **THE TĀMÎD** (הַתָּמִיד hat-tāmîḏ 'the continual [offering]') = the twice-daily burnt-offering (morning + evening, per Exod 29:38-42; Num 28:3-8). **HISTORICAL FULFILLMENT**: Antiochus IV's edict (15 Kislev 167 BCE, per 1 Macc 1:54-59) abolished the *tāmîd* and erected the 'desolating sacrilege' (cf. 9:27, 11:31, 12:11) on the altar. Qere-ketiv: הרים/הוּרַם.

verses.text: וְצָבָ֛א תִּנָּתֵ֥ן עַל־הַתָּמִ֖יד בְּפָ֑שַׁע וְתַשְׁלֵ֤ךְ אֱמֶת֙ אַ֔רְצָה וְעָשְׂתָ֖ה וְהִצְלִֽיחָה׃
verses.translit: wə-ṣāḇāʾ tinnāṯēn ʿal-hat-tāmîḏ bə-p̄āšaʿ wə-ṯašlēḵ ʾĕmeṯ ʾarṣāh wə-ʿāśə-ṯāh wə-hiṣlîḥāh
verses.notes: **The host was given over to it together with the continual burnt offering through transgression; and it cast truth to the ground, and it acted and prospered.** Textually difficult — the host-given-over and the transgression-clause are syntactically ambiguous. The 'truth cast to ground' = Torah suppressed.

verses.text: וָאֶשְׁמְעָ֥ה אֶֽחָד־קָד֖וֹשׁ מְדַבֵּ֑ר וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֶחָ֨ד קָד֜וֹשׁ לַפַּֽלְמוֹנִ֣י הַֽמְדַבֵּ֗ר עַד־מָתַ֞י הֶחָז֤וֹן הַתָּמִיד֙ וְהַפֶּ֣שַׁע שֹׁמֵ֔ם תֵּ֛ת וְקֹ֥דֶשׁ וְצָבָ֖א מִרְמָֽס׃
verses.translit: wā-ʾešməʿāh ʾeḥāḏ-qāḏōš mə-ḏabbēr way-yōmer ʾeḥāḏ qāḏōš lap-palmōnî ham-məḏabbēr ʿaḏ-māṯay he-ḥāzōn hat-tāmîḏ wə-hap-pešaʿ šōmēm tēṯ wə-qōḏeš wə-ṣāḇāʾ mirmās
verses.notes: **Then I heard a holy one speaking; and another holy one said to the one that spoke: 'For how long is the vision concerning the continual burnt offering, the transgression that makes desolate, and the giving over of the sanctuary and host to be trampled?'** **THE HOLY ONES IN DIALOGUE** = angelic council. **TERM**: הַפֶּשַׁע שֹׁמֵם (hap-pešaʿ šōmēm 'the transgression that desolates') — a variant of the 'abomination of desolation' formula. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Dan 9:27, 11:31, 12:11 (variations on the formula); cf. Matt 24:15 + Mark 13:14 ('the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet'). **THE 'HOW LONG' QUESTION** is the classic apocalyptic angelic-dialog form (cf. Zech 1:12; Rev 6:10).

verses.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י עַ֚ד עֶ֣רֶב בֹּ֔קֶר אַלְפַּ֖יִם וּשְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת וְנִצְדַּ֖ק קֹֽדֶשׁ׃
verses.translit: way-yōmer ʾēlay ʿaḏ ʿereḇ bōqer ʾalpayim ū-šəlōš mēʾōṯ wə-niṣdaq qōḏeš
verses.witness_tertiary: OG: 2400 evenings-mornings; Theodotion: 2300, agreeing with MT. The textual variation reveals early uncertainty about the exact number.
verses.notes: **He said to me: 'For two thousand three hundred evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary shall be restored to its rightful state.'** **THE 2300 EVENINGS-MORNINGS** — אַלְפַּיִם וּשְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת ʿereb bōqer. **CRITICAL CALENDAR-CRUX**: scholars divide on whether this is (a) 2300 days (literal reading of 'evenings-mornings' as days, cf. Gen 1's day-language) ≈ 6.32 years; or (b) 2300 half-days (each 'evening-morning' = one *tāmîd* offering, two per day) = 1150 days ≈ 3.16 years. **HISTORICAL FIT**: option (b), 1150 days, fits most precisely the duration from Antiochus IV's first interference with the temple (per 1 Macc 1:20-24, mid-169 BCE) to the rededication on 25 Kislev 164 BCE — approximately 1150 days. Option (a) is favored by some (per Goldingay 1989) and fits a longer count from earlier persecution-events. **'NIṢDAQ'** (וְנִצְדַּק) = 'be restored / vindicated / re-justified' — the Hanukkah rededication (1 Macc 4:36-59; 2 Macc 10:1-8). Cross-reference: 7:25 (time/times/half-a-time = 3.5 years) + 8:14 (2300 evenings-mornings) + 12:7 (time/times/half) + 12:11 (1290 days) + 12:12 (1335 days) — the Daniel calendar-arithmetic problem.

verses.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּרְאֹתִ֛י אֲנִ֥י דָנִיֵּ֖אל אֶת־הֶחָז֑וֹן וָאֲבַקְשָׁ֣ה בִינָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד לְנֶגְדִּ֖י כְּמַרְאֵה־גָֽבֶר׃
verses.translit: way-hî bi-rʾōṯî ʾănî Dāniyyēʾl ʾeṯ-he-ḥāzōn wā-ʾăḇaqšāh ḇînāh wə-hinnēh ʿōmēḏ lə-neḡdî kə-marʾēh-ḡāḇer
verses.notes: **When I, Daniel, had seen the vision, I sought to understand it; and behold, there stood before me one having the appearance of a man.** **כְּמַרְאֵה־גָבֶר** (kə-marʾēh-ḡāḇer 'as the appearance of a man') — anticipates v 16 where the figure is named Gabriel. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Ezek 1:26 ('a likeness as the appearance of a man'); cf. Rev 1:13 ('one like a son of man').

verses.text: וָאֶשְׁמַ֥ע קוֹל־אָדָ֖ם בֵּ֣ין אוּלָ֑י וַיִּקְרָא֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר גַּבְרִיאֵ֕ל הָבֵ֥ן לְהַלָּ֖ז אֶת־הַמַּרְאֶֽה׃
verses.translit: wā-ʾešmaʿ qōl-ʾāḏām bên ʾŪlāy way-yiqrāʾ way-yōmar Gaḇrîʾēl hāḇēn lə-hallāz ʾeṯ-ham-marʾeh
verses.notes: **I heard the voice of a man between the banks of the Ulai, and it called, 'Gabriel, make this man understand the vision.'** **GABRIEL** — גַּבְרִיאֵל (Gaḇrîʾēl 'God-is-my-strength') — **FIRST NAMED ANGEL IN HEBREW BIBLE**. Reappears in 9:21. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: cf. Luke 1:11-20 (Gabriel announces John the Baptist's birth to Zechariah); Luke 1:26-38 (Gabriel announces Jesus's birth to Mary — the Annunciation) — Gabriel's NT role as messenger of the messianic births directly continues his Daniel role as interpreter of the messianic-time-table. cf. 1 En 9:1, 20:7, 40:9 (Gabriel as one of the seven archangels). The 'voice from the Ulai' (third party) calling Gabriel signals a higher-ranking divine speaker.

verses.text: וַיָּבֹא֙ אֵ֣צֶל עָמְדִ֔י וּבְבֹא֣וֹ נִבְעַ֔תִּי וָאֶפְּלָ֖ה עַל־פָּנָ֑י וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ הָבֵ֣ן בֶּן־אָדָ֔ם כִּ֖י לְעֶת־קֵ֥ץ הֶחָזֽוֹן׃
verses.translit: way-yāḇōʾ ʾēṣel ʿomdî ū-ḇə-ḇōʾō niḇʿattî wā-ʾeppəlāh ʿal-pānāy way-yōmer ʾēlay hāḇēn ben-ʾāḏām kî lə-ʿeṯ-qēṣ he-ḥāzōn
verses.notes: **He came near where I stood; and when he came, I was frightened and fell upon my face; but he said to me: 'Understand, O son of man, that the vision is for the time of the end.'** **בֶּן־אָדָם** (ben-ʾāḏām 'son of man') — Daniel is here addressed as 'son of man' — the standard Ezekielian address-form (Ezek 2:1 et al.). NOTE: this 'son of man' is distinct from the Aramaic *bar ʾĕnāš* of 7:13 (an exalted figure); here it is Daniel-as-mortal. **'TIME OF THE END'** (עֵת קֵץ ʿēṯ qēṣ) — the eschatological terminus. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. 1QS 4 + 1QM (Qumran end-time-terminology); cf. Mark 13 + Matt 24 (the eschatological discourse).

verses.text: וּבְדַבְּר֣וֹ עִמִּ֔י נִרְדַּ֥מְתִּי עַל־פָּנַ֖י אָ֑רְצָה וַיִּ֨גַּע־בִּ֔י וַיַּֽעֲמִידֵ֖נִי עַל־עָמְדִֽי׃
verses.translit: ū-ḇə-ḏabbərō ʿimmî nirdamtî ʿal-pānay ʾārṣāh way-yiggaʿ-bî way-yaʿămîḏēnî ʿal-ʿomdî
verses.notes: **As he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face to the ground; but he touched me and set me on my feet.** **THE PROPHETIC TRANCE** + ANGELIC TOUCH-RESTORATION: cf. Ezek 1:28-2:2 ('I fell on my face... and a spirit set me on my feet'). cf. Rev 1:17 ('I fell at his feet as though dead; but he laid his right hand on me').

verses.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הִנְנִ֣י מוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֔ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיֶ֖ה בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַזָּ֑עַם כִּ֖י לְמוֹעֵ֥ד קֵֽץ׃
verses.translit: way-yōmer hinənî mōḏîʿăḵā ʾēṯ ʾăšer-yihyeh bə-ʾaḥărîṯ haz-zāʿam kî lə-mōʿēḏ qēṣ
verses.notes: **He said: 'Behold, I will make known to you what shall be at the latter end of the indignation; for it pertains to the appointed time of the end.'** **'THE INDIGNATION'** (הַזָּעַם haz-zāʿam) = the period of divine wrath = the Antiochene persecution. **'APPOINTED TIME OF THE END'** (לְמוֹעֵד קֵץ lə-mōʿēḏ qēṣ) — appears here, 11:27, 11:35.

verses.text: הָאַ֥יִל אֲשֶׁר־רָאִ֖יתָ בַּ֣עַל הַקְּרָנָ֑יִם מַלְכֵ֖י מָדַ֥י וּפָרָֽס׃
verses.translit: hā-ʾayil ʾăšer-rāʾîṯā baʿal haq-qərānāyim malḵê Māḏay ū-P̄ārās
verses.notes: **'The ram which you saw with the two horns, these are the kings of Media and Persia.'** **EXPLICIT IDENTIFICATION** — Media and Persia. This explicit naming undermines (per Collins) the four-kingdom reading that separates Media and Persia in ch 2/7 (the dominant scholarly four-kingdom scheme: Babylon-Media-Persia-Greece, with the fourth = Greece/Seleucids). Conservative Christian reading sees Medo-Persia as one (matching ch 8) and identifies fourth = Rome.

verses.text: וְהַצָּפִ֥יר הַשָּׂעִ֖יר מֶ֣לֶךְ יָוָ֑ן וְהַקֶּ֤רֶן הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֵּין־עֵינָ֔יו ה֖וּא הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃
verses.translit: wə-haṣ-ṣāp̄îr haś-śāʿîr meleḵ Yāwān wə-haq-qeren hag-gəḏōlāh ʾăšer bên-ʿênāyw hūʾ ham-meleḵ hā-rîšōn
verses.notes: **'And the male goat is the king of Greece; and the great horn between his eyes is the first king.'** **EXPLICIT IDENTIFICATION** — יָוָן (Yāwān) = Greece/Ionia. The first king = Alexander the Great. **NOTE**: this is the most explicit prediction of Greco-Macedonian kingdom in the HB; combined with the Antiochus IV details (vv 23-25), it is the foundation for the scholarly consensus that the visions are *vaticinia ex eventu* composed during/after the Antiochene crisis (167-164 BCE), per Collins 1993, Newsom 2014, Hartman-DiLella 1978.

verses.text: וְהַ֨נִּשְׁבֶּ֔רֶת וַתַּֽעֲמֹ֥דְנָה אַרְבַּ֖ע תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ אַרְבַּ֧ע מַלְכֻי֛וֹת מִגּ֥וֹי יַעֲמֹ֖דְנָה וְלֹ֥א בְכֹחֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wə-han-nišbereṯ wat-taʿămōḏnāh ʾarbaʿ taḥtêhā ʾarbaʿ malḵuyōṯ mig-gōy yaʿămōḏnāh wə-lōʾ ḇə-ḵōḥō
verses.notes: **'As for the horn that was broken, in place of which four others arose, four kingdoms shall arise from his nation, but not with his power.'** Confirmation of the four Diadochi reading.

verses.text: וּֽבְאַחֲרִית֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔ם כְּהָתֵ֖ם הַפֹּשְׁעִ֑ים יַעֲמֹ֛ד מֶ֥לֶךְ עַז־פָּנִ֖ים וּמֵבִ֥ין חִידֽוֹת׃
verses.translit: ū-ḇə-ʾaḥărîṯ malḵūṯām kə-hāṯēm hap-pōšəʿîm yaʿămōḏ meleḵ ʿaz-pānîm ū-mēḇîn ḥîḏōṯ
verses.notes: **'And at the latter end of their rule, when the transgressors have reached their full measure, a king of bold countenance, one who understands riddles, shall arise.'** **THE 'KING OF BOLD COUNTENANCE'** = Antiochus IV Epiphanes ('Epiphanes' = 'manifest [god]'; contemporaries punned to 'Epimanes' = 'mad-one'). **'UNDERSTANDS RIDDLES'** (מֵבִין חִידוֹת mēḇîn ḥîḏōṯ) = skilled in intrigue/duplicity.

verses.text: וְעָצַ֤ם כֹּחוֹ֙ וְלֹ֣א בְכֹח֔וֹ וְנִפְלָא֥וֹת יַשְׁחִ֖ית וְהִצְלִ֣יחַ וְעָשָׂ֑ה וְהִשְׁחִ֥ית עֲצוּמִ֖ים וְעַם־קְדֹשִֽׁים׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿāṣam kōḥō wə-lōʾ ḇə-ḵōḥō wə-nip̄lāʾōṯ yašḥîṯ wə-hiṣlîaḥ wə-ʿāśāh wə-hišḥîṯ ʿăṣūmîm wə-ʿam-qəḏōšîm
verses.notes: **'His power shall be great, but not by his own power; and he shall cause fearful destruction, and shall succeed in what he does, and destroy mighty men and the people of the saints.'** 'Not by his own power' = his power is divinely-permitted, not autonomous. 'People of the saints' = the Torah-observant Jews under Antiochene persecution.

verses.text: וְעַל־שִׂכְל֗וֹ וְהִצְלִ֤יחַ מִרְמָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ וּבִלְבָב֣וֹ יַגְדִּ֔יל וּבְשַׁלְוָ֖ה יַשְׁחִ֣ית רַבִּ֑ים וְעַ֤ל־שַׂר־שָׂרִים֙ יַעֲמֹ֔ד וּבְאֶ֥פֶס יָ֖ד יִשָּׁבֵֽר׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿal-śiḵlō wə-hiṣlîaḥ mirmāh bə-yāḏō ū-ḇi-lḇāḇō yaḡdîl ū-ḇə-šalwāh yašḥîṯ rabbîm wə-ʿal-śar-śārîm yaʿămōḏ ū-ḇə-ʾep̄es yāḏ yiššāḇēr
verses.notes: **'By his cunning he shall make deceit prosper under his hand, and in his own mind he shall magnify himself; without warning he shall destroy many; and he shall even rise up against the Prince of princes; but, by no human hand, he shall be broken.'** **'PRINCE OF PRINCES'** (שַׂר־שָׂרִים śar-śārîm) = YHWH himself, OR Michael (as 'prince of princes' parallel to 12:1 'great prince'). **'BY NO HUMAN HAND'** (בְּאֶפֶס יָד bə-ʾep̄es yāḏ) — divine, not human, destruction. **HISTORICAL FULFILLMENT**: Antiochus IV died in 164 BCE on campaign in Persia of disease (per Polybius 31.9; 1 Macc 6:1-16; 2 Macc 9) — not killed by human hand. Cross-corpus to 8:25-26 (2300 evenings-mornings calendrical-arithmetic).

verses.text: וּמַרְאֵ֨ה הָעֶ֧רֶב וְהַבֹּ֛קֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר נֶאֱמַ֖ר אֱמֶ֣ת ה֑וּא וְאַתָּה֙ סְתֹ֣ם הֶֽחָז֔וֹן כִּ֖י לְיָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃
verses.translit: ū-marʾēh hā-ʿereḇ wə-hab-bōqer ʾăšer neʾĕmar ʾĕmeṯ hūʾ wə-ʾattāh səṯōm he-ḥāzōn kî lə-yāmîm rabbîm
verses.notes: **'The vision of the evenings and the mornings which has been told is true; but seal up the vision, for it pertains to many days hence.'** **'SEAL UP THE VISION'** (סְתֹם הֶחָזוֹן səṯōm he-ḥāzōn) — apocalyptic-pseudonymity device: the vision is portrayed as preserved for a far-future audience (which is the 'real' audience reading it during Antiochene persecution). **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Dan 12:4, 12:9 (the sealed book); cf. Rev 22:10 ('do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near') — Revelation reverses the Daniel seal-instruction, signaling proximate fulfillment.

verses.text: וַאֲנִ֣י דָנִיֵּ֗אל נִהְיֵ֤יתִי וְנֶֽחֱלֵ֙יתִי֙ יָמִ֔ים וָאָק֕וּם וָאֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה אֶת־מְלֶ֣אכֶת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וָאֶשְׁתּוֹמֵ֥ם עַל־הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה וְאֵ֥ין מֵבִֽין׃
verses.translit: wa-ʾănî Dāniyyēʾl nihyêṯî wə-neḥĕlêṯî yāmîm wā-ʾāqūm wā-ʾeʿĕśeh ʾeṯ-məleʾḵeṯ ham-meleḵ wā-ʾeštōmēm ʿal-ham-marʾeh wə-ʾên mēḇîn
verses.notes: **And I, Daniel, was overcome and lay sick some days; then I rose and went about the king's business; but I was appalled by the vision and did not understand it.** Daniel's physical collapse after the vision — the cost of apocalyptic-receiving on the seer. The 'king's business' is presumably Belshazzar's court-work; the chronological tension with the chs 5-6 framing is part of the book's non-linear narrative-arc.
